questions.topic: Common Table Expressions for Readable Query Pipelines
questions.question: What is a common table expression?
options: A named query result scoped to one SQL statement
A permanently stored table with an independent lifecycle
A database index created for every selected column
A session-wide cache guaranteed to be physically materialized

questions.topic: Common Table Expressions for Readable Query Pipelines
questions.question: What should a well-named CTE make visible?
options: Only the sequence number assigned by the author
The semantic stage and grain represented by its rows
The exact physical join algorithm the engine must use
A guarantee that its result is persisted to storage

questions.topic: Common Table Expressions for Readable Query Pipelines
questions.question: A CTE filters query-document rows, and a second groups them by model_version. What grain does the second CTE have?
options: One row per original query-document pair
One row for the complete database
One row per model version
One row per selected SQL expression

questions.topic: Common Table Expressions for Readable Query Pipelines
questions.question: Why is assuming a CTE always materializes unsafe?
options: SQL forbids engines from storing any intermediate result
A CTE is always a permanent table rather than a query expression
Materialization occurs only when the CTE has no selected columns
Optimizers may inline or materialize it depending on engine and plan

questions.topic: Common Table Expressions for Readable Query Pipelines
questions.question: A costly intermediate must be reused across several statements and audited independently. What is the strongest choice?
options: Materialize it explicitly as a temporary or persisted table
Repeat an unnamed nested expression in every statement
Assume one CTE definition remains available after its statement ends
Use SELECT star so the optimizer must cache every source column

questions.topic: Common Table Expressions for Readable Query Pipelines
questions.question: Why should CTE stages project required columns rather than pass SELECT star everywhere?
options: Projection forces every CTE to change its grain
It clarifies valid attributes and avoids moving unused bytes
SELECT star guarantees that schemas never evolve
Projection prevents any execution plan from inlining the CTE

questions.question: What makes a subquery correlated?
options: It contains an aggregate function
It appears inside a WHERE clause
It references a column from the current outer row
It returns exactly one scalar value

questions.question: How is an uncorrelated subquery logically evaluated?
options: Once for every outer-row key using that key as a filter
Only after the outer query has returned all rows
As a recursive reference to its containing SELECT
Independently because it uses no outer-row columns

questions.question: What does a correlated EXISTS query preserve when selecting documents with failed chunks?
options: Document grain, with each qualifying document returned at most once
Chunk grain, with one document copy for every failed chunk
Global aggregate grain, with one row for all documents
Failure-status grain, with document identifiers discarded

questions.question: Why can a correlated subquery be slow for a million outer rows?
options: Correlation guarantees one constant-time indexed probe per row
If not decorrelated or indexed, large inner work may repeat per outer row
Correlated queries cannot contain a WHERE predicate
The outer rows must be globally sorted after each inner comparison

questions.question: When can correlated indexed probes beat pre-aggregating a huge inner table?
options: When the outer set is huge and every probe scans the full inner table
When no index exists and the inner predicate uses a volatile function
When the outer set is small and each probe is a cheap keyed lookup
When the scalar subquery returns several rows for every outer record

questions.question: An uncorrelated scalar AVG subquery receives no non-NULL input and returns NULL. What does score > that result do?
options: It treats NULL as zero and retains every positive score
It reruns AVG once for every score until a value appears
It converts score into a grouping key and returns one row
It evaluates UNKNOWN and filters rows unless a fallback is defined

questions.topic: UNION vs UNION ALL and Duplicate Semantics
questions.question: What does UNION ALL do with duplicate rows?
options: It preserves them while concatenating branch results
It removes them within and across every branch
It retains only the duplicate with the largest key
It raises an error whenever two rows compare equal

questions.topic: UNION vs UNION ALL and Duplicate Semantics
questions.question: What additional operation does UNION perform?
options: A keyed latest-wins merge based on update time
Exact-tuple deduplication over the combined rows
A guaranteed final sort by every selected column
A join between rows sharing the first selected value

questions.topic: UNION vs UNION ALL and Duplicate Semantics
questions.question: Daily partitions are guaranteed disjoint by date. Which operator best combines two days?
options: UNION, because every partition must be re-deduplicated
INNER JOIN, because dates define matching row pairs
UNION ALL, because concatenation preserves the proven disjoint rows
FULL JOIN, because branch columns align only through keys

questions.topic: UNION vs UNION ALL and Duplicate Semantics
questions.question: Rows share query_id and document_id but have different scores. Why will UNION retain both?
options: UNION compares only the first selected column
UNION always preserves every duplicate row
Scores are excluded automatically from duplicate comparison
Duplicate identity covers the full selected tuple

questions.topic: UNION vs UNION ALL and Duplicate Semantics
questions.question: Overlapping retry exports disagree on ingestion time. What is the correct way to choose one row per business key?
options: UNION ALL followed by explicit keyed ranking and a latest-wins rule
UNION over every column, which makes differing timestamps equal
SELECT star with no source or precedence information
LIMIT one on each branch before comparing business keys

questions.topic: UNION vs UNION ALL and Duplicate Semantics
questions.question: Why is SELECT star risky in set-operator branches?
options: Set operators align values by column alias rather than position
Schema evolution can change positional alignment or make branches incompatible
SELECT star forces UNION ALL to deduplicate every output row
Set operators require each branch to have different column counts
